Chinese traditions of disciplined attention provide a meaningful vocabulary for this question without specifying a neural mechanism. F116 asks whether a goal is still available after a declared delay. A recall probe must distinguish the identity of the goal, the cue that might trigger it, and the opportunity to perform it. Enumerate all eligible goal trials and record the actual interval, including interruptions and independent reminders. A prompted response must not be counted as unaided retention. Future investigators should preserve the distinction between commitment and memory. A participant may decline an action while remembering it perfectly. A negative study must remain publishable, and no result should be used to judge character or willpower. Learning in the presence of error F117 treats expectation and outcome as separable events. In a bounded task, a signed discrepancy may influence a subsequent prediction. A classical stochastic or strategic model can account for many apparent learning trajectories; quantum terminology is not necessary to describe them. Record predicted and observed outcomes before calculating error. Randomize the sign and timing of perturbations, and compare a frozen update rule with a no-learning, mean-reverting, and explicit-strategy alternative. A fitted rate in inverse trials is not an anatomical measurement. A successor can challenge the error definition itself. If the presumed error is actually clock delay, a response to instruction, or selective timeout coding, the rate must be withdrawn or relabeled. The corrected design is valuable even when the original interpretation fails. Persons rather than averages F118 asks which variation in adaptation is reproducibly person-specific. A group mean does not describe every learner. Yet apparent individual diversity may reflect noisy measurement, different exposure histories, task ceilings or the selection of participants who remain. Repeated pretraining and training observations help separate measurement error from within-person and between-person variation. Record verified exposure, context and calibration; use partial pooling and held-out person-level evaluation rather than ranking from a single change score. Personalized language must not harden uncertain estimates into identity. A model should report the uncertainty of a person's predicted trajectory, with no obligation to accept a label. If the variation cannot be reconstructed, use a pooled estimate or abstain. The meaning of an hour F119 defines dose as measured practice rather than elapsed clock time. The philosophical idea of measured effort can inspire a test of diminishing returns, but neither a cultural maxim nor an apparent plateau specifies the optimal duration of exercise. Separate active minutes, instruction, warm-up, breaks and elapsed days. A dose constant in hours can be identified only if the sampled range and observation scale distinguish competing curves. tittel: Flagship 51/90 Held-out task-transfer effect after training is the preregistered question, not a demonstrated effect. VOLITION TRAINING AND QIGONG NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL COUPLING AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Acupuncture Trilogy, Family II, develops the research question of transfer of learned physiological self-regulation to genuinely untrained tasks. Its core three-coupling is Volition training x qigong practice x neural plasticity. The scope is non-invasive recordings with voluntary, ethics-approved participation; no treatment intervention. Ancient and contemporary philosophical terms are treated as research motivation and operational labels, not independent proof of physical forces or of treatment benefit. The candidate proposal asks whether held-out task-transfer effect after training can be measured with transparent source identities and enough precision to distinguish the proposed account from instrument practice and familiarity rather than transferable neurophysiological learning. A prospectively frozen evaluation would test concealed reassignment of task order and an unfamiliar outcome instrument; stronger conventional comparisons include time-matched cognitive training and attention-control practice. Stop when improvement exists only on the rehearsed scoring task, when calibration fails, or when a study lacks appropriate permission. Aborted and negative outcomes remain part of the full eligibility denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical research plates examine distinct modeling and verification roles with explicit units, assumptions and blind counterexamples. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations. Two hundred Research Gates frame distinct pairings of a target readout, orthogonal check, concealed challenge, rival account and refusal decision. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instruments, evidence contracts and cross-laboratory research tools. This content is prospective research design and contains no completed experimental outcomes. The source study contract is the STARLI 90 Flagship Master v1.3. Methodological ancestry supplied in that document includes DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.23480803, 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 and 10.5281/zenodo.23318840. These methods do not validate the new candidate; bibliography and individual formula suitability still require independent external checking. Full English PDF. Automated structure and lexical difference checks cannot establish scientific originality, causal validity or clinical efficacy. Two species, Mansonia uniformis and Mansonia septempunctata, which breed in association with macrophytes such as water hyacinth Eichhornia crassipes, became less common from stage 1 to 2. The saltmarsh species Aedes vigilax was also collected in reasonable numbers at all localities around the reservoir. This species is known for its wide dispersal powers and was undoubtedly blown in from the extensive intertidal wetlands on the coast. Thus on the basis of abundance, two taxa – Culex annulirostris and Anopheles annulipes s.1. – warranted further consideration. The former species is considered to be the major vector of arboviruses in Australia (Russell 1995), transmitting Ross River, Barmah Forest, Kunjin, Kokobera, Alfuy and Edge Hill viruses and Murray Valley encephalitis, as well as dog heartworm. Of these, Ross River is by far the most common arbovirus in coastal northern Queensland, with morbidity approximating 400 cases per 100,000 population. Thus from first principles, this arbovirus and perhaps Barmah Forest, about which little is known, would constitute the greatest hazard to recreational use. Although Anopheles annulipes has previously been implicated in malaria transmission at Sellheim during the Second World War, this species group has returned isolated positives of Ross River and Barmah Forest viruses and Murray Valley encephalitis from other parts of Australia. However, no transmission studies have been done on the population from the reservoir. Thus on the evidence to date, it could not be regarded as a major concern at the Ross River dam. Both Culex annulirostris and Anopheles annulipes were shown to have seasonal peaks of abundance during the late post-wet season (March to May), with populations building up with the onset of spring (September to October). Spatially, the trapping programme was designed to compare mosquito numbers on the foreshore of the stage 1 lake with two localities expected to be on the margins of the stage 2A lake, with two remote localities (and therefore theoretically unaffected by any water resource project activity) as negative controls. Mosquito numbers (i.e. for those species known to breed at the dam) decreased with distance away from the Ross River dam. Both light trapping and human bait collections carried out twice per month were reasonable indicators of broad seasonal trends in mosquito abundance. However, the statistical analysis indicated that occasionally the light traps could miss short periods of high biting activity (Jones et al. 1991). If greater resolution was required, it was recommended that light traps could be supplemented with animal baited traps, although it is probable that this could be rectified by intensifying the light trapping regimen. Cluster analyses of dam breeding species in both 1984–85 and 1991–93 indicated that light trap catches along the northern (Big Bay, Ti-Tree Bay, Round Island) and western sides (Ross River) gave similar patterns, but the profile towards the east (Antill Creek, Toonpan, Oak Valley) was somewhat different (Barker-Hudson et al. 1993; Hearnden and Kay 1995). On this basis, adult mosquito surveillance would therefore need to be based on two localities at either end of the lake.
